content.title: About
content.content: Stevia powder is a natural sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant. The powder is intensely sweet (up to 300‑400 times sweeter than sugar) while providing virtually zero calories and a low glycemic index. It is used in cooking, baking, beverages, and diet recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Stevia originates from South America, where indigenous peoples used it long before colonization.
Its sweetness comes from steviol glycosides, which are not metabolized by the human body.
Unlike sugar, stevia does not raise blood glucose levels, making it suitable for people with diabetes.
Stevia has been granted GRAS status in the US and approved by EFSA in Europe.
The powder dissolves easily in hot and cold liquids, though high amounts may leave a slight aftertaste.

items.title: Low Calorie
items.content: Stevia provides virtually no calories, helping to control overall energy intake.

items.title: Blood Sugar Support
items.content: Steviol glycosides do not cause glucose spikes, which is beneficial for pre‑diabetes and type 2 diabetes.

items.title: Antioxidant Properties
items.content: Steviol glycosides exhibit antioxidant activity, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Blood Pressure Reduction
items.content: Some studies suggest regular stevia consumption may contribute to modest blood pressure lowering.

items.title: Oral Health
items.content: Stevia does not promote tooth decay and may reduce bacterial growth in the mouth.

items.title: Allergic Reactions
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergy to stevia; discontinue use if symptoms appear.

items.title: Aftertaste
items.content: High doses can produce a bitter or licorice‑like aftertaste that not everyone finds pleasant.

items.title: Medication Interactions
items.content: Stevia may enhance the effect of antihypertensive drugs; consult a physician if you take such medication.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add stevia powder to tea, coffee, smoothies, yogurts, sauces, and baked goods. When substituting sugar, a typical ratio is 1 g stevia to 10 g sugar, but adjust to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store stevia powder in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent moisture absorption and flavor loss.
